newsitem.title: USA: Ethics panel sends Gingrich tape to Justice Dept..
newsitem.headline: Ethics panel sends Gingrich tape to Justice Dept..

text.p: The senior Democrat on the House ethics committee on Monday turned over to the panel an audiotape of a controversial telephone call by House Speaker Newt Gingrich, but the committee said it forwarded the tape to the Justice Department.

A Florida couple on Monday said they made the audiotape of the conversation between Gingrich and his top lieutenants and passed it on to Rep. Jim McDermott of Washington, who has declined comment on the matter.

Theodore Van Der Meid, chief counsel for the ethics committee, sent McDermott a letter late on Monday saying the panel had hand delivered the tape and the accompanying cover letter to the Justice Department.

"This is to notify you that the material you sent to the committeee at 4:33 p.m. this afternoon was not accepted. By direction of the chair and after consultation with the chief of the criminal division of the Department of Justice, the contents of the envelope including the audio cassette tape and the cover letter were hand delivered to the Department of Justice this evening," the letter said. A copy of the letter was released to Reuters.

A transcript of the tape, which Democrats said showed that Gingrich was violating a pledge not to orchestrate his public defense in the ethics case, was published in two newspapers two days after the Florida couple handed the tape to McDermott.

Republicans have called for an FBI criminal investigation into the source of the leak. The conversation between Gingrich and some of his top lieutenants took place on Dec. 21, the day the ethics committee said Gingrich had violated House rules and he admitted doing so.
